While the player is standing still or is moving slower than their maximum running speed,The maximum running speed refers to player's horizontal movement speed, which has a base value of 3 pixels and can be changed through movement speed bonuses. However, this value is not changed by accessories like Hermes Boots, as they instead override the player's movement speed. The player can enter stealth as long as both their horizontal velocity and vertical velocity are at least 0.1 pixels slower than their maximum running speed. they quickly enter stealth, which causes them to turn almost invisible and prevents Fighter AI and Flying AI enemies from firing projectiles at the player while they are not using an item. Stealth is gradually built up over the course of ceil(1/0.015) ticks.
During the first ceil((1/0.015)*0.25) ticks of building up stealth, the player gains several stat boosts that linearly increase to the following maximum values, and keep these maximum values if the player builds up further stealth beyond that point:
+50% ranged damage
+10% ranged critical strike chance
−750 aggro
The player also gains the following stat boost, which linearly increases to its maximum value over the full ceil(1/0.015) ticks duration of building up stealth:
+50% ranged knockback

The number of charges built is indicated by a shield that appears in front of the player, with two and three spikes appearing on the shield, corresponding with the charge count.
Taking damage depletes one charge and creates an explosion called Solar Radiance around the player.
While there is at least one charge built, the player can activate a special dash attack by double-tapping either the Left Click or Right Click key. Striking an enemy with the dash damages it and causes a damaging Solar Radiance explosion, so enemies always take damage twice. A Solar Blaze charge is consumed if at least one enemy was hit. The dash has a 1-second cooldown.
Furthermore, the Solar Blaze buff provides +20% damage reduction, regardless of the number of charges. Combined with the base damage reduction from the armor's set bonus, it grants a total of 29.6% damage reduction.
Each piece equipped (even if hidden by vanity items) causes the player to emit light, with a higher light level for each additional piece equipped. Additionally, equipping the full set causes the player to emit pulses and afterimages while moving.
